newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares higher on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares higher on selective buying.

text.p: Delhi shares traded higher in afternoon trade on Thursday as selective buying by domestic and foreign investors more than offset selling by operators, brokers said.
The Delhi sensitive index was up 1.02 points at 796.68.
"Major players are eagerly waiting for P. Chidambaran to join the new government as finance minister before resuming buying," said Roshan Sethi of brokers Share Point.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral won a parliamentary vote of confidence on Tuesday, ending more than three weeks of political uncertainty.
Gujral retained most ministers who served in the previous government, but Chidambaram was not sworn in following a decision of his Tamil Maanila Congress to stay out of the government.
Hindustan Lever added 19 rupees to 1,079, boosted by foreign buying.
State Bank of India fell 2.30 rupees to 307.50.
